newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NBP gives primary dealer standings for Oct.
newsitem.headline: Polish NBP gives primary dealer standings for Oct.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland said the country's top 15 banks' average share in secondary T-bill and NBP-bill trade fell to 4.2 percent each in October from 4.6 percent in September, the central bank said.
The NBP also said the average daily T-bill holdings of domestic non-banking sector clients in October was 4.2 percent in each of the banks, down 0.1 point from September's level.

Both figures are elements of the NBP's money market dealer scheme, in which banks get points for activity on secondary markets and increasing the financing of the budget deficit by the domestic non-financial sector. @

The central bank will likely pick the top 15 banks in the scheme in December and make only them eligible to participate in its open market operations next year. Now 29 banks are allowed to take part in open market operations with the NBP.
